policies.title: Container runs privileged
policies.description: Checks that no container sets privileged: true.
policies.rationale: A privileged container has nearly the host's power and is a direct escape path.
policies.remediation: Remove privileged: true; add only the specific capability needed.
references: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards (public)
NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance (public; not opened in this research, UNVERIFIED)
policies.positive:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: reg.example/app:1.2.3
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
policies.negative:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: reg.example/app:1.2.3
        securityContext:
          privileged: false

policies.title: Containers may gain more privileges than their parent
policies.description: Checks that every container sets allowPrivilegeEscalation: false.
policies.rationale: Set-uid binaries could otherwise raise privileges inside the container.
policies.absence_note: Default for allowPrivilegeEscalation is true, so a container that does not set it fails.
policies.remediation: Set allowPrivilegeEscalation: false on each container.
references: Kubernetes Pod Security Standards (public)
NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance (public; not opened in this research, UNVERIFIED)

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: a
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: reg.example/app:1.2.3
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
policies.negative:

policies.title: Containers are not required to run as non-root
policies.description: Checks that runAsNonRoot: true is set at pod level or on every container.
policies.rationale: Root in a container is far easier to turn into a node compromise.
policies.absence_note: Not set means the image's user is used, which may be root: treated as a failure (the Restricted standard asks for an explicit setting).
policies.remediation: Set securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true and a numeric runAsUser.

policies.title: Container adds a powerful Linux capability
policies.description: Checks that capabilities.add does not include ALL or other near-root capabilities.
policies.rationale: These capabilities enable host-level actions and escapes.
policies.remediation: Add only the minimal capability required, such as NET_BIND_SERVICE.

NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guidance (public; not opened in this research, UNVERIFIED)

      containers:
      - name: app
        image: reg.example/app:1.2.3
        securityContext:
          capabilities:
            add: ["SYS_ADMIN"]

policies.title: Containers do not drop all capabilities
policies.description: Checks that every container drops ALL capabilities.
policies.rationale: Fewer capabilities, smaller escape surface.
policies.absence_note: Without a drop list the runtime default capability set is kept: treated as a failure.
policies.remediation: Set capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] and add back only what is needed.
